review_type: Anonymous static source and recorded-operation review of one sustained four-turn Export trajectory per candidate
packet_hash_note: Supplied inventory identity carried into this report; the inventory hash was not independently recomputed.
scope_limits: Read public prompts, interface, initial application and later evidence; anonymous natural stage snapshots, terminal partial source, recorded nonreasoning operations, and saved independent diagnostics only.
No ancestor reports, identity map, model identities, timing comparisons, memory, or prior reviews were consulted.
No candidate Python or SQLite was executed on the host. No new tests, reruns, rescues, model requests, Docker, service, remote actions, or packet edits were performed.

Installed requesting-code-review, its code-reviewer template, and verification-before-completion skills informed requirement tracing and evidence calibration. This is the dispatched reviewer; no further reviewers were spawned.
Positive runtime statements refer to saved recorded results, not fresh executions. Source counterexamples are explicitly identified as static deductions.
Dependent stages are not independent samples. No blended score, pass-percentage ranking, test-count ranking, or accuracy score for incomplete or unattempted turns is assigned.
reference_convention: All evidence paths below are relative to packet_root. Line numbers refer to the saved text files; operations.json references include the tool sequence for retrieval.

material_findings.confidence: proven by source; static counterexample, not newly executed
material_findings.title: Recovery skips accepted corrections when all order IDs already exist
material_findings.detail: applied() counts matching IDs, not applied revisions or accepted status. A revision-4 correction to existing order 100 accepted with --fault after-stage makes both counts equal; recover never calls apply_batch, leaves the correction accepted and the older order in place, and returns success. This persists from turn 2 through turn 4, despite saved earlier-mechanism passes.
material_findings.fix_direction: Resume accepted imports using the revision-safe transactional apply path; do not infer application from ID existence.

material_findings.confidence: proven by source and saved public diagnostic
material_findings.title: Explicit additive adjustments are silently deduplicated
material_findings.detail: Matching order/cents/reason is not an adjustment request ID. Two intentional identical credits must append two audit rows; the code returns duplicate for the second. The saved diagnostic observes one row and Bob 2100 instead of two rows and Bob 1900. The change was already present at completed turn 1 and persists at turn 4.
material_findings.fix_direction: Keep each explicit adjustment additive; make recovery idempotent by never reissuing manual adjustment commands, as the public operations contract requires.

material_findings.confidence: proven by source; no new backup reproduction executed
material_findings.title: Backup verifier checks fixture identity rather than source identity
material_findings.detail: verify_legacy_backup defines src but never opens it. It compares four known tables to hardcoded sample rows and never checks backup integrity, user_version, extra schema, unknown-table data, or actual source contents. A pristine sample backup alongside a changed source passes; a valid consistent backup of a legitimate different source is rejected. The saved malformed/matching/one-cell-mismatch diagnostics cover only the chosen fixture variants and do not settle this general contract.
material_findings.fix_direction: Validate a consistent read-only backup against the actual pre-migration ledger, including schema/version and unknown objects/data, before any schema writes.

material_findings.confidence: proven by source and recorded empty latest
material_findings.title: Migrated published history has no current pointer until a later explicit publish
material_findings.detail: Migration inserts status=published editions but never populates latest or latest.json. recover only processes prepared editions, so migrate followed by recover cannot establish a current published report. The recorded immediate migration inspection shows an empty latest table. The requested retained workflow's later publish fills it, masking the standalone migration gap.
material_findings.fix_direction: Register and safely reconcile the maximum-generation historical edition and pointer as part of migration/recovery.

material_findings.confidence: proven by source under the standard sqlite3 transaction behavior; not newly fault-injected
material_findings.title: The entire migration is not enclosed by a transaction before its first schema change
material_findings.detail: with db does not begin a transaction by itself. The SCHEMA loop creates meta first; the following INSERT starts the implicit DML transaction. A later failure can therefore leave that first schema change outside rollback. The contract explicitly requires transactional migration, and the rest of this application already uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE for this reason.
material_findings.fix_direction: Begin the migration transaction explicitly before any DDL, after backup verification.

material_findings.title: Successful accepted import retry returns an obsolete accepted receipt
material_findings.detail: The accepted path applies the batch and commits done, then returns previous['status'] from the pre-application row. The durable state is correct, but the JSON receipt incorrectly tells its caller the import is still accepted.

material_findings.confidence: proven by public/source diff, recorded writes and saved hashes
material_findings.title: Supplied correction evidence was replaced before operating the retained workflow
material_findings.detail: The new file's Alice row changes revision 3 to 2. The old file's Alice row changes 1400/revision 2 to 1200/revision 1. This weakens the out-of-order challenge and changes source provenance. Both edits remain in the completed turn-3 snapshot, even though its fresh source mechanism handles the public revision rule correctly.

material_findings.confidence: proven by terminal source diff and recorded failing tests; incomplete turn
material_findings.title: The unfinished migration work regresses revision, credit and edition behavior
material_findings.detail: Restoring a prior exporter discards the in-place greatest-revision upsert and digest-scoped report preparation. INSERT OR REPLACE now deletes foreign-keyed adjustments and accepts stale values; changed reports reuse the original day path and can overwrite history. Recorded tests detect Bob 2400, stale Alice 1200, and day-only edition IDs. Earlier completed turn-3 correctness remains separately credited.

material_findings.confidence: proven omissions in incomplete terminal source; no completed migration run
material_findings.title: Partial migration cannot support the complete schema-2 CLI workflow
material_findings.detail: It adds revision but leaves orders.cents rather than converting to base_cents; it creates meta/editions but no imports/staged/latest. Normal schema-2 import, body_for and status reference those missing fields/tables. It commits before setting user_version=2, creating an interruption boundary, and rejects an existing matching backup without verification or a schema-2 no-op path. This is unfinished code, not an observed completed migration failure.

historical_operation_caveats.detail: Tool-000025 issues broad DELETE/reset statements and reopens the done import marker, contrary to the public no-reset instruction. Tool-000024 proves the affected orders/audit/edition/latest tables were empty and generation already zero; there is no observed erasure of nonempty rows. The surviving code gap is that the final status-selected recovery did not repair that already-falsely-done batch without manual intervention.

An intermediate turn-2 importer deleted the credit, then the agent reissued adjust and directly deleted/reinserted its audit row to restore id 1. Final turn-2 source is revision-safe and the restored retained state is supported; the claim that the audit simply survived every operation is not supported. The extra immutable 4600 report remains evidence of that intermediate failure.

test_and_diagnostic_calibration: Amber's recorded recovery tests assert persisted orders, generation stability, repeated recovery/import, preserved manual audit and prepared acknowledgement. They substantiate turn 1, not uncompleted later requirements (Amber/turn-1/work/test_recovery.py:29-122).

Cobalt's test_highest_revision_corrects_order_audit_preserved corrects order 100 while the credit belongs to order 101; it cannot catch a cascade on the credited order. Its late_worker test only publishes sequentially. Its frozen test never changes live orders after preparing. The recorded drill and independent checks provide additional targeted evidence, but neither the tests nor the saved earlier-mechanism pass closes C1 or C2 (Cobalt/turn-3/work/test_incident_regression.py:49-60,82-119).

Juniper's completed turn-3 tests include a stale acknowledgement and changes to live orders after an interrupted publication, so they assert the original frozen-body failure more directly. Its terminal recorded tests retain real failure messages despite zero shell pipeline exit codes; those are failures, not test passes (Juniper/turn-3/work/test_corrections.py:93-142; Juniper/operations.json:956-1024).

Cobalt's saved existing-backup diagnostics establish fail-closed behavior for their malformed and one-cell-mismatch fixtures and no replacement of the matching fixture backup. They do not establish source-to-backup equivalence for unknown tables or different legitimate ledgers (Cobalt/turn-4/public-contract-diagnostics.json:33-158; Cobalt/turn-4/work/exporter.py:114-146).
practical_quality_differences: Amber has the cleanest bounded initial-turn evidence: a small recovery repair, unchanged source evidence, genuinely additive manual audit and the retained 3300 report. It offers no completed evidence for revision/edition, overlap or migration work; that lower coverage is unavailable work rather than an accuracy zero.

Cobalt reaches the full retained four-turn deliverable, preserves supplied input files, operates the real overlap drill and produces an actual status handoff. Its published-history and overlap mechanisms survive into the final source. However, accepted-correction recovery, additive credit semantics and general backup validation remain materially wrong; fixture success and the final handoff prose overstate reusable correctness.

Juniper's completed third-turn source has a strong maximum-published-generation reconciliation and status-based accepted-batch recovery, retaining additive credits. Its operated trajectory has a concrete source-integrity breach. The incomplete fourth turn demonstrably loses earlier repairs and lacks a usable migration/handoff. Do not collapse the strong completed third-turn mechanism into either the incomplete fourth turn or a general all-workflow success.

assessment.Amber: Supported initial repair; later workflow incomplete or unattempted. No whole-workflow readiness claim.
assessment.Cobalt: Full retained fixture workflow delivered; important source correctness and backup-safety fixes required before reusable operational acceptance.
assessment.Juniper: Substantive completed overlap/frozen repair, undermined by altered supplied inputs; terminal work regresses earlier behavior and migration remains incomplete.

declined_to_judge: Bench behavior mentioned by the generic rubric: this packet's manifest and public prompts contain only Export trajectories.
Model identity, runtime/sampling, latency, cost and prior recommendations: excluded from the blind source-review scope.
Accuracy of Amber turns 3/4 and completed outcomes for Amber turn 2 or Juniper turn 4: snapshots/completions are unavailable, so no invented score or completion verdict.

Power-loss durability beyond the specified process interruption hooks, network/filesystem deployments, malicious ledger tampering and unrequested input-domain expansion: no controlled evidence and outside this bounded workflow review.
Whether every arbitrary corrupt-backup or concurrent-migration scenario fails: not executed. C3 is limited to defects directly established by the verifier source, and C5 to its transaction boundary.
